title: Redo and front/back answer to the chords graphic editors use
detail: Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ are what a designer already has in their fingers. The redo audit found the opposite: Ctrl+Shift+Z would have undone.
check: pressed the documented chords with a selection made, and read the object order before and after each

title: An undo crossing an image no longer deletes it
detail: The image's persisted src was an object URL revoked at decode, so Fabric could not enliven it on restore and dropped the object — one undo deleted the asset. Revocation moved to session end. NOTE: the user later corrected the framing — the underlying complaint was that transformations never entered history, and this fixed the restore path rather than that. See vg-030.
check: imported an image, moved it, undid, and confirmed the image was still on the canvas

title: Entering a group makes only that group's objects selectable
detail: "You are inside a group" lived in grouping-manager's context array and only the layer panel read it, so the artboard contradicted the list. Worse, editor-shell routed every double-click into enterGroup, so double-clicking a text box to edit it recorded a group context.
check: entered a group and counted selectable objects: 1 of 51, where before it was 51 of 51

title: The trends chart is no longer the only aliased one
detail: MAX_BACKING_PIXELS clamped the largest chart to 1.53x while every smaller one got 2x, so the only aliased graph was the one a reader looks at longest.
check: compared rendered pixels per chart at equal scale; every chart now samples at the same multiple

title: An inserted object is named, and the name round-trips
detail: Without this, every object an author created was a uuid in the layer list, permanently.
check: inserted a shape, named it, saved the package, and read the name back out of the zip

title: The glass control renders on every object and says why where it cannot apply
detail: The user's own test found the first version incomplete: "The checkbox is unselectable but the tooltip only show when tabbed, not mouse hovering." aria-disabled rather than disabled, because a disabled control leaves the tab order and the reason would reach a mouse and nobody else.
check: selected a Line, tabbed to the glass control, and read what a screen reader announces: the control, and the reason it is unselectable

title: A bounded number field clamps onto its bound and carries a native slider
detail: "Took me a while to figure out blur only accepts 48 maximum." The field passed min: 0 and no max, so it had no slider and nothing to clamp onto. The user's first test said neither existed.
check: typed 60 into the glass blur field and read the field, the object and the new slider: 48, blurRadius 48, range min 0 max 48

title: Glass works on Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon
detail: Ruled by the user. Polyline, Path and Line are excluded — an open path has no interior to sample. A prior attempt to read this as "clamping proven nearby" is why the check names the shapes.
check: frosted a Circle, an Ellipse, a Triangle and a Polygon in the built editor and read each clip: the frosted patch follows the shape, not the bounding box

title: The player's failure screen names the cause, not a JavaScript parse error
detail: It printed V8's SyntaxError verbatim on a wall display, which is both meaningless to a reader and misleading — it says the theme file is corrupt when the likeliest cause is that nothing is serving.
check: pointed the player at a missing theme and read the screen: "The host did not answer with a theme — it may not be running."

title: A POSIX root volume joins its own drive
detail: library-devices stripped a trailing slash, turning / into "", and compared fs against mount. On Windows the path is C: and the strip is a no-op, so the suite was green and the whole platform was broken.
check: a test with a volume at / on a device that also holds /data; before, disk.total was undefined

title: A theme is a folder; a ZIP is only what an author exports
detail: Ruled twice by the user. The list() call was decompressing every package in the library to print N lines, and a 33 MB asset saved successfully and then 404'd. The window between two renames could also make a theme look deleted.
check: saved a theme from the real editor and read the folder: theme.json, assets/, thumbnail.png beside it

title: A saved theme can be read back by id
detail: Before, the editor could not open a saved theme at all: rename, save, reload /editor/, and the edit was gone. A save is a write-only surface with no way back to it.
check: renamed a theme, saved it, opened /editor/?theme=<id> in a fresh document, and read the saved name; a dead id falls back to the default

title: A stale save is refused rather than applied over someone else's work
detail: Two editors on one theme: the second save was built from a document that predated the first, and won silently.
check: three writes through the real API: current base 200, no base 200, stale base 409, and the stored theme unchanged after the 409

title: An unchanged save writes and uploads nothing
detail: documentKey boxed one JS number per asset byte and stringified it — 1,614 ms and 86 MB retained, on every open, new and save. The key now holds the envelope and each declared digest.
check: three saves of one theme with a 438 KB asset: the first request carried 1,169,576 bytes of asset data, the two unchanged saves carried zero

title: The two disk dropdowns stop asking the same question
detail: "Which device should dashboards use?" appeared twice, and the legend was the only thing telling them apart — and a legend scrolls out of view.
check: opened the two disk dropdowns on the settings page and read both prompts: they name different drives

title: The Arrange menu is gone; the toolbar above the canvas already had all eight
detail: Ruled by the user: the menu was redundant with the toolbar, not a drift to be synced. An agent was dispatched to make the menu offer all eight before the ruling arrived; it was killed with nothing committed.
check: read the menu bar in the live editor: File, Edit, Insert, View; the toolbar has 8 arrange buttons

title: A crop control is reachable for a selected image
detail: The crop manager was constructed, wired to history, and never called — 4.6 kB of tested code with no entry point. Found while correcting a claim about image history.
check: selected an image in the built editor, opened Crop, and read the session: aspect presets, Apply and Cancel

title: Delete removes an object from the collection that holds it
detail: canvas.remove searches canvas._objects, so a grouped child was never found — and the manager returned true and saved a scene identical to the one before, so nothing anywhere disagreed.
check: grouped two objects, selected a child, pressed Delete, and read group._objects: the child left

title: Reordering no longer moves a grouped object into the canvas collection
detail: All four ordering actions left the child in BOTH collections — same reference — so Fabric painted it twice and the scene serialised it twice. The binding is Ctrl+Shift+], not Ctrl+].
check: pressed Ctrl+Shift+] three times on a grouped object, then serialised: 51 top-level objects and the child once, not twice

title: The starter theme's charts render in the player, gauges included
detail: Fixed in 7904424 on 2026-09-28; what was missing was the evidence — the stack had never been kept. ECharts 6.1.0's _renderPointer reads _progressEls inside a data-diff callback assigned only after a render that drew an arc. Player-only: it renders before telemetry arrives and flips progress.show under a datum already present.
check: counted distinct colours in each chart own ECharts canvas on a real host: ram-gauge 6 to 57, vram-gauge 6 to 45, track ink flat

title: Double-clicking outside an entered group does not exit it; only Escape does
detail: "double clicking outside a group didn't exit it, only the Esc key does." editor-shell.ts binds mouse:dblclick to enterGroupOnDoubleClick — enter only. Nothing on screen says Escape is the way out. Neither fixed nor recorded until the user tested for it.
check: Fix reverted: 2 of 6 dblclick tests fail. Live: entered a group by double-click (3 rows in context, 50 dimmed), then double-clicked empty canvas and the group context cleared - q1-group-entered.png vs q1-group-exited.png.

title: Locked and unlocked icons are hard to tell apart; locked should be a filled lock
detail: "Locked and unlocked icons in the layer panel is visually hard to distinguished. Locked should use a filled lock icon, not an outline icon like unlocked." The layer panel already has a KIND_ICONS pattern to follow. Small.
check: Reverted fix: the filled-lock test fails. In the built editor the locked row renders a solid padlock among outline ones - q1-lock-icons-zoom.png.

title: A locked object should stay selectable on the canvas, just not movable
detail: "Locked icon should still be selectable in the canvas, it just can't be transformed, moved. Otherwise user will have to go hunt for it in the layer panel." selectable: false is currently how a locked object is prevented from being transformed, and the same flag is what makes it unselectable — the same split the group fix made once.
check: Reverted fix: 5 of 7 lock tests fail. Live on a locked object: hasControls false and every lock* flag set, a 120px drag moved it 0px, 8 arrange actions disabled, and a shift-click alongside an unlocked object left it out of the selection - q1-locked-selected.png.

title: The drag-select marquee vanishes when the mouse pauses rather than releases
detail: THE ROWS HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG and the real cause is worse. Not bound to pointerup: the marquee is drawn straight onto the canvas context by Fabric, is not part of the scene, and every full repaint erases it. The editor repaints the whole scene 30 times a second (editor-main starts startChartRefresh at rate 30), so the marquee survived about 33ms — one frame — and was then gone until the pointer moved again. That is exactly the reported symptom: flashing during a drag, gone when the pointer stops. The editor now holds the refresh for the duration of a pointer gesture. Live readings are not worth showing mid-drag anyway, and the first frame after mouse:up brings them current.
check: Reverted fix: the browser test fails with the upper canvas reading 0, i.e. no marquee at all after a 600ms pause. With the fix the same read is non-zero. Live by hand on a rebuilt bundle: held the pointer still mid-drag for 1.8s and the marquee is still drawn (vg-027-fixed-held.png), where before the pause it was absent (vg-027-held.png); CPU readings resumed after release, 26% then 41% then 46%.

title: The crop notice contradicts the geometry it describes
detail: WITHDRAWN — the notice was right and the report was my instrument error. Fabric anchors .left/.top, it does not read them as a box: a theme that omits originX/originY revives at originX center, so the object box runs -60.5 to 140.5 while the glyph run is at -60.5 to -38.5, genuinely off a 1920 artboard. The real defect found alongside it — a revived display had no artboard boundary at all, so objects painted over the letterbox bars while the notice said they were not shown — is fixed in 299c0bf, which added artboard-clip and artboard-crop coverage and the persist.ts boundary. Kept rather than deleted because the mistake is the reusable part: a notice that disagrees with the geometry is usually the reader, and the way to tell is to check which one Fabric actually honours.

title: Every unmatched host path serves the player
detail: CAUSE ESTABLISHED, and it was not the fallthrough itself but serveStatic: an extension-less path was treated as a client route and fell back to the bundle index.html, so /play and /display resolved to the dashboard. A file with an extension never took that branch, which is why /theme.json had always 404d while /nope returned 200 with a live display. The editor needs its fallback — it is a client-routed app under /editor — and the player does not: it is one document, so only "/" may fall back. serveStatic now takes that as a parameter, true at the editor mount and false everywhere else. ADR-0018 already claimed this path, so the 404 that answers now says Not found. rather than a build hint that is not true.
check: Reverted fix: the new test fails on expected 200 to be 404 for /play. Live against a rebuilt host: /?data=live and /favicon.svg serve 200, while /play, /display, /nope and /theme.json all answer 404 Not found. 43 host tests pass.

title: A text object's Height field shows a stale measurement before the author has authored a height
detail: REFUTED as stated, and the search beside it found something worse. The Height field is NOT stale: on a freshly inserted Text it read 79 for a measured 78.83, and after a longer run wrapped inside a 64-unit box it read 463 for a measured 462.85 — it tracks the measurement exactly. The real defect is one field away and is vg-057. The original claim is kept above because the refutation is the useful part: a field that follows a measurement is not reporting a stale one.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: the Height field read 79 against a measured 78.83, then 463 against 462.85 after the run wrapped. Reverted against the half-box it did not produce: see vg-057.

title: A palette token's key and the name an author sees are different strings, and that is by design
detail: MEASURED on the built editor, three colours added in a row. Keys: colour, colour-2, colour-3. Names: New colour, New colour, New colour — and renaming the second to "CPU brand" left its key at colour-2 and the list showing "CPU brand · 0". So the reported shape is real and the defect it was filed as is not: the key is an internal id that §75 already rules is never renamed, and it NEVER REACHES THE AUTHOR. document.body.innerText contains neither colour-2 nor colour-3; they appear only as select value attributes in the HTML. The layer list shows the name, which is the string a person typed. The one residue worth keeping: every added colour carries the identical default name New colour, so three of them are indistinguishable until the author renames each.
check: Live in the built editor: after three adds the token select reads colour, colour-2, colour-3 while the visible labels read New colour, CPU brand, New colour, and a body-text scan for colour-2 and colour-3 returns nothing. Renaming moved the label and left the key alone, which is the id contract rather than a defect.

title: A text run could not be told not to print its unit, so the author got the unit twice
detail: REFUTED AS WRITTEN, and the real gap is narrower and now closed. The mechanism always existed: formatValueSegment reads run.unitDisplay ?? binding.unitDisplay, and the reference theme uses it — measured on the shipped Starter, cpu-card-value is a value run on cpu.load with unitDisplay none plus a literal % at the caption size, and its canvas text reads 47%, one percent sign. What did not exist was a control. unitDisplay was on the CHART bindings panel and absent from the TEXT RUN panel, so an author who wanted the reference pattern had no way to author it: set a reading and the unit printed itself, add a literal % beside it and the unit printed twice. REPRODUCED BY HAND on the rebuilt editor: set the run to Short and cpu-card-value renders 69%%, set it back to None and it renders 64%. The run panel now carries the same four options the chart panel has, Default/None/Short/Long. It writes the RUN rather than the binding, because a run own unitDisplay takes precedence — writing the binding is silently shadowed by exactly the theme this control exists to reproduce, which the first version did.
check: Red without the control: the new test fails with TypeError reading a null select. With it, 26 run-panel tests pass, and live in a rebuilt editor the run reads 47% at None, 69%% at Short and 64% back at None — the doubled unit, produced and then prevented by the control.

title: The background media is declared as an asset and has no layer
detail: WITHDRAWN as a duplicate — this is vg-030 for one kind of asset, and the row said so itself. MEASURED to confirm it is still true: the Starter declares starter-backdrop as its background media and paints it full-bleed, the layer list has 52 rows and NOT ONE of them is the backdrop, and the canvas holds 52 objects of which zero are images. The media is declared, rendered and unaddressable, which is the same defect vg-030 carries for assets generally. Tracked once, in vg-030. The GitHub issue is closed with this row named.
check: Live in the built editor: 52 layer rows and 0 of them match backdrop/media/background/image; 52 canvas objects and 0 are images, while the theme settings declare starter-backdrop as Background media. Confirms the duplicate rather than the closure — the underlying defect stays open in vg-030.

title: Delete cannot remove an object that lives inside a group
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry. FIXED in 82eef78 — see vg-018. Kept here so the issue and the registry agree; close the issue against vg-018.

title: The Ctrl+N discard prompt times out waiting for a Discard button
detail: THE ROW WAS RIGHT AND IT WAS A TEST DEFECT, in three places rather than one. REPRODUCED: reference-theme.spec.ts times out on waiting for a Discard button inside a dialog that is already visible — because the dialog it found was the artboard SIZE CHOOSER, which has Cancel and Create. Measured by hand on the running editor: Ctrl+N on a changed document opens Choose an artboard size; the question about the changes, Save changes before opening another theme?, arrives only after Create is pressed. The test looked for Discard one step too early. The second failure was also stale: it asserted the scene still held the reference composition after New, but New is a blank theme of the chosen size and the reference is the separate New from starter command — measured, the canvas holds 0 objects after Create and Discard. The third was the status copy, New Fabric theme against the products New theme. All three call sites now go through one answerDialogIfShown helper that WAITS for the dialog rather than asking is it up right now, which is what an async dirty guard made unanswerable.
check: Red before, green after. The test was waiting on the Discard button inside a dialog that was already visible, because the dialog it found was the artboard size chooser with Cancel and Create; pressing Ctrl+N twice is what reaches the discard prompt. With the helper it passes in 15.5s, the two dialog tests in editor.spec.ts still pass, and npm run lint is clean with no isVisible().catch races left in tests/e2e.

title: The crop frame is drawn a whole image up and to the left of the image it frames
detail: A Rect is anchored at its centre but getBoundingRect() reports a corner, so the frame begin() built sat at twice the offset: its top-left was the image top-left, putting the frame up and to the left by one full image width and height. Three of its four edges, and the crop handles on them, fell off the canvas, so the session read as a frame that could be grown but never cropped. Owner: crop-manager/index.ts begin().
check: Reverted fix: the crop-frame test fails on origin left/top. The frame bounding rect now equals the image bounding rect left, top and size.

title: The display tells a reader it has 30 sensors when it reads 19
detail: MEASURED on the Starter served by a live host: the stream was requested with 30 key entries covering 19 distinct sensors (cpu.load three times, gpu.load three, ram.used.percent three, and six more twice), and the availability strip read "2 of 30 sensors have no reading". startHostedTheme built its key list with a flat map and no Set, while the two other call sites that answer the same question — the editor private semanticKeys in editor-main.ts and requiredSemanticKeys for a ThemeDocument — both dedupe. The hosted path is the one a real deployed display takes, so the count a wall reader sees is inflated by how many objects happen to bind the same reading. The repeat request is the same defect: the display asks for the same sensor three times a second and nothing new comes back.
check: Reverted fix: 2 of 3 bound-keys tests fail. Live on the served Starter after a player rebuild: the stream requests 19 distinct keys with no repeats, and the strip reads 2 of 19 sensors where it read 2 of 30 - vg-053-sensor-count.png.

title: A missing file is reported as a bundle that was never built
detail: serveStatic sent one message for every file it failed to read, so "The player bundle is not built. Run: npx vite build packages/player" answered requests for a theme.json, a package zip and a stale chunk alike. MEASURED against a host with both bundles built: /theme.json, /assets/theme.zip, /assets/nope.js, /editor/assets/nope.js and /editor/nope.html all returned 404 with that text. The message is the one AGENTS.md itself sends people chasing, so following it rebuilds a bundle that is already there and returns the identical answer — the failure mode is a loop, not a delay. The message now says Not found. once the bundle entry exists, and the build hint is reserved for the case it is true of. ADR-0018 records why no static server upstream solves this shape.
check: Reverted fix: the built-bundle test fails on "expected the player bundle is not built not to contain is not built". Live against a rebuilt host with both bundles present: /theme.json, /assets/nope.js and /editor/assets/nope.js all answer 404 Not found., while / and /editor/ still serve.

title: A pasted image and a new group are listed by their uuid instead of a name
detail: MEASURED in the built editor: pasting a PNG added a row reading image-d8032a9b-438c-4a46-8d1e-b469d3fdad16, and grouping two cards added group-<uuid>, while an inserted Rectangle read Rectangle. object-name.ts states the contract plainly — absence of a name means fall back to the id — and the id of a freshly minted object is a uuid, so the two creators that set no name are the two the fallback cannot help. image-manager and grouping-manager were the only creators not going through newObjectName, whose own comment already named this failure. Both now call it; the words Image and Group live in ui-copy beside text and panel, where newObjectName already reads them.
check: Reverted fix: both tests fail on expected undefined to be Image and undefined to be Group. Live in a rebuilt editor: a pasted image row reads Image and a group built from a canvas shift-click multi-select reads Group, where both previously printed a 42-character id.

title: Filling in one Size field left half an authored box, and the text object lost its width
detail: MEASURED, and it destroys the object. A text inserted by the editor has no authored box — its width is Fabric measurement until an author types one. Typing 120 into Height wrote vigiliaText.box as { height: 120 } with no width; the merge in selection-inspector was correct, the box it merged into did not exist. The next text change made authoredBox multiply an undefined width by the scale, and the object ended with width null and getBoundingRect() returning nulls — unrenderable, unselectable by geometry, and no longer savable. Fixed by seeding both dimensions from the object own measured edge, so the first Size field an author fills in produces a whole box.
check: Reverted fix: the new test fails on expected undefined to be 126.21875, the measured width. Live on a rebuilt editor, the same sequence that ended at width null now reads width 63.8 and a bounding rect of 100x379, with vigiliaText.box holding both dimensions - vg-042-box-width.png.

title: Entering a group did not dim the layer list until something else re-rendered it
detail: MEASURED on the built editor: group two cards, double-click into the group, and 0 of 53 rows carry data-context. Click any row and 3 light up while 50 drop to opacity 0.45. CAUSE ESTABLISHED and it is not Fabric forgetting: entering a group does not move the selection. The group is already the active object, so setActiveObject is a no-op and MEASURED: zero of the four canvas events the bridge republishes on fire at all. The layer panel therefore never learns the context changed and keeps whatever projection it had. The manager now announces the context on the editor:group-context-changed canvas event — the custom editor: convention the other managers already use — and the bridge listens to it alongside its four.
check: Reverted fix: the announcement test fails on expected [] to have a length of 1. Live on a rebuilt bundle with real gestures: entering the group gives 3 rows in context and 50 dimmed, and double-clicking empty canvas returns to 0 and 0. 139 tests across the grouping and shell suites pass.

title: A chart's series colours and its bindings are coupled by index, so removing a middle binding shifts the colours
detail: MEASURED ON THE REFERENCE THEME, then fixed. The per-series paint is a positional array sitting beside the bindings, and removing a binding filtered the bindings without touching the paint. Measured on trends-chart: palette [cpu, gpu, ram] with bindings [trends-cpu, trends-gpu, trends-ram]; remove the MIDDLE one and the palette became [cpu, gpu] while the bindings became [trends-cpu, trends-ram] — so the RAM series painted with the GPU green. Nothing on screen looked wrong; the chart simply told a different story. seriesPaintFor already reconciled the arrays lengths and its truncation is right for the LAST binding, which is why the case nobody tries passes. The manager now carries each surviving series own paint through the removal before the length fix runs, so a middle removal keeps cpu and ram. Adding is unchanged: a new series repeats the last colour, which is what extending a chart means.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: trends-chart reads [palette.cpu, palette.gpu, palette.ram] before and [palette.cpu, palette.ram] after removing gpu.load, where it read [palette.cpu, palette.gpu] before the fix and painted RAM green. Two unit tests: carriedPaintFor pins the middle, the last and the unchanged case, and the panel test pins that the three Remove buttons name their reading and remove only their own. NOT PINNED: the one-line call from #writeBindings into carriedPaintFor — the manager-level test needs a panel harness this file does not have, and I did not build one. That wiring rests on the live measurement above, not on a test.

title: The palette colour field accepts anything, and persists it
detail: FIXED AT THE SOURCE, and the validator was not the gap. Measured first: the palette colour field accepted rebeccapurple, not-a-colour, #GGG and rgb(1,2,3) with no alert and checkValidity() reporting the field valid — and the published validator is no tighter, because validateGlobals checks the entry id, the name, that a value exists and that there are no unknown keys, and never looks at a colour. So the file the editor wrote passed its own schema because the schema has no rule. The field now asks the browser, which already holds the answer: CSS.supports("color", value) is the same engine that will paint it, so there is no second hand-written list of colour names to keep in step. A value the engine rejects is refused with the browsers own validity message naming it, and not committed — which matters because ctx.fillStyle keeps the PREVIOUS colour for an unparseable one, so accepting it meant the edit silently did nothing while the document carried the nonsense. STILL OPEN, deliberately: whether a CSS keyword such as rebeccapurple belongs in the vocabulary is a decision about which words the product accepts, not about correctness, and nothing here settles it. Upstream of vg-031 stays true — a picker does not fix a write path that does not check.
check: Red without the guard: the browser test fails on validity.valid expected false received true. Live in the built editor: #123456 commits, not-a-colour leaves the field invalid with a message naming it, and after the panel redraws from the palette the field reads #123456 again — the refused value was never committed. jsdom has no CSS object, so this can only be pinned in a browser; the unit suite cannot cover the predicate.

title: A selected Line shows a diagonal bounding box instead of two end handles and a rotate handle
detail: BUILT, after the search in ADR-0020 and a correction to it. A Line now carries two endpoint controls and the rotation handle — endpointA, endpointB, mtr — and no bounding box at all: hiding the six handles it does not need would have left the box, which is the defect. Each endpoint reads its own corner from x1/x2 and y1/y2 rather than assuming top-left and bottom-right, because width and height are absolute: measured on a line drawn right-to-left, the same two numbers are the other pair of corners. Moving an end writes that end and leaves the other where it was. Shift holds the line at a multiple of 15 degrees, on a modifier that branches in exactly one unrelated place. THREE THINGS THE ROW AND THE NOTE GOT WRONG, all found by measuring rather than reading. ONE: this projects Line is x1, y1, x2, y2 — four scalars, no points, no pathOffset, no setDimensions — so Fabric polyline controls and the anchor technique that go with them do not apply to it; nothing in snap-manager reads either representation, so snapping was never going to understand an endpoint for free. TWO: writing x2 makes Line re-derive left/top, so reading the objects own matrix back on every mousemove mapped each step through a frame the previous step had already moved — measured, the handle landed about 1.6x where it was dropped and a purely horizontal drag raised the far end by 188 units. The gesture frame is now taken once at mouse-down. THREE, and it is the one that would have shipped: Line.ownDefaults resolves up the prototype chain to the object every Fabric object shares, so assigning controls onto it took the handles off rectangles and text boxes too. Caught by an existing handle-size test, and assigned as a new defaults object now.
check: Red without the controls: all three new tests fail, the first on the control names. Live in a rebuilt editor: a selected Line reads endpointA, endpointB, mtr; a textbox, a rect and a chart each still read all nine with mtr. Dragging the far end 100 canvas px at 0.374 zoom moved x2 by 266.7 against 267.1 expected — 0.06 percent — with x1 and y1 unchanged, and with Shift held the line settled at 15.0 degrees. Editor suite 1041 across 84 files.

title: The Performance Trends panel does plot; the empty reading was a five-second-old source
detail: REFUTED, and the row own hypothesis was the right one. Measured against a live host rather than the preview source, after 18 seconds: history() over a 60-second window returns 42 points for each of cpu.load, gpu.load and ram.used.percent, every one status ok, and the panel draws all three lines - vg050-trends-live.png. The earlier reading of zero keys came from the PREVIEW source after 5 batches and 7 seconds, which is exactly the explanation the row offered when it filed itself as a measurement rather than a finding: chartPlaybackDelayMs exists on the source, so playback simply had not filled the window yet. The pass repeated mistake is closing here: two sessions read an empty source as a broken chart, and the thing that separated them was waiting longer and reading a real telemetry source, which is what this row said to do.
check: Live on a host streaming real telemetry: 42 points in the 60s window for each of the three series, latest 39.2, 30 and 83.6 percent, all status ok, and the panel draws three lines. The strip beside it reads 2 of 19 sensors have no reading, which is the LibreHardwareMonitor gap and not this.

title: The Starter was reported as edited the moment it opened
detail: FIXED, and the cause was not what two earlier readings of this row guessed. isDirty compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and the document differed from itself. THE INSTRUMENT THAT SETTLED IT, built in jsdom because a browser probe could not reach it: mount the Starter, snapshot, run one live pass, snapshot, and report the differing JSON paths. THE ANSWER IS styles. One pass rewrites .scene.objects.N.styles[M] on 18 of the Starter 52 objects — exactly its binding count — with nothing touched. styles is Fabric per-character formatting; the authored truth for a bound text object is vigiliaText.runs, and the renderer resolves runs into styles and text. documentKey now compares the document with those two renderings removed, on the objects whose runs are the authored truth; an object without runs owns its text and styles and keeps them. The asset half was fixed separately and is in the same commit — it enumerated the loaded byte map, so the key depended on how much had loaded rather than on what the document declares. NOT text, as I first assumed: stripping text alone changed nothing, and I reverted that rather than ship a key transform on an unproven hypothesis that could hide a real edit.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: Ctrl+N then Create on an UNTOUCHED Starter no longer asks to save. It still asks after inserting a Rectangle, and still asks after editing a text run by hand. Red without the fix: the shell test fails on isDirty expected false received true. 20 tests across the shell and persistence suites.

title: An asset in use cannot be removed — and that is told to the author, not swallowed
detail: THE FOUR DEFECTS MEASURED, AND THREE OF THEM ARE NOT DEFECTS. (1) Replace allocates a new path per import: REFUTED. With a PNG selected, replacing it with a different PNG left the list at two entries and kept the same key, so it replaces in place and the key an author sees does not move. (2) and (3) the layer list being inconsistent and some assets showing while some do not: REAL, and one thing, which is vg-047 folded in here as its duplicate — measured, the Starter declares starter-backdrop, the artboard uses it as its background media, and the canvas document mentions NEITHER asset while the layer list has 53 rows and names no asset at all. (4) some assets cannot be removed: REFUTED, and the opposite of swallowed. Pressing Remove on the one asset the artboard is using leaves it in place and says That asset is in use and cannot be removed — the panel guards on a reference check and reports it. I first read this as a silent no-op because I was reading the editor status footer instead of the panels own alert line; the button is enabled, the click does something, and the something says why. NOTHING WAS FIXED HERE because there was nothing to fix: what survives is the layer-list gap, which is the row that was already carrying vg-047.
check: Live on the Starter: Remove on starter-backdrop leaves the list at one and reports That asset is in use and cannot be removed. Replace on a selected PNG keeps the list at two and the same key. backgroundMedia is starter-backdrop while the layer list names no asset and the canvas document mentions neither.

title: The palette colour field has a picker that keeps alpha
detail: BUILT on shadcn, per the ruling that this fields ecosystem is shadcn/ui rather than Base UI; that ruling supersedes the plans 2026-09-29 search, which reached the opposite conclusion, and the plan is annotated so the question is not re-litigated. WHAT IT IS: a popover with four tracks — saturation, brightness, hue and alpha — over a checkerboard so a translucent token reads as translucent, a hex field for exact entry, and a swatch trigger beside the existing text field, which stays because a value can be typed exactly and a picker cannot always be dragged to it. Everything is 8-digit hex, which is what the envelope stores. WHY NOT A NATIVE INPUT, which is the requirement that rules the obvious answer out: input type=color has no alpha channel and the themes paints carry it — panel is 85 percent and frost is 30 percent — so accepting one would be a way to lose the value. THE COST, STATED ONCE: shadcn components are Radix-based, so this adds a second headless library beside Base UI, plus clsx, tailwind-merge and cva. The user ruled with that cost in view. The maths is a pure module with its own tests, away from the DOM: it caught two of my own bugs — alpha scaled as if it were a 0-255 channel, turning 85 percent into 1/255, and a regex capture passed where the parsed alpha belonged, producing NaN in the hex.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor, dragging each track in turn: hue on white leaves it white (correct — hue cannot move a colour with no saturation), saturation gives #26ff3c, brightness gives #137f1e, and alpha gives #137f1e66 with the field and the hex readout agreeing. The token name survives a colour change. 5 maths tests, and the editor suite is 1049 across 85 files.

title: A gradient is edited on a track, with the colour picker on every stop
detail: BUILT on the pickers parts, which is what the row asked for: one picker per stop rather than a second colour vocabulary. A gradient was angle plus an offset and a colour per stop, as three number fields and a free-text box, with nothing to look at while editing it. There is now a preview of the gradient it produces, a track whose handles are its stops, and the shared shadcn picker on each. The number fields stay because a drag cannot land on 0.37 exactly and an author who wants exact entry still can. THE STOP COUNT IS NOT CAPPED AT TWO, which is what ruled out the Cladd ColorEditor in the plans search — the track is driven by the stop array and the panel adds stops itself. WHAT THE BUILD LEARNED: the pickers were first behind a click that opened the chosen stop picker, and it never worked, because the palette panel rebuilds its own DOM on every redraw and React state naming this stop is open was destroyed by the next commit — the popover would have closed on the very pick that applied it. They are inline per stop instead, which needs no state and is the better behaviour anyway. As with vg-031 the surface is shadcn on Radix, per the ruling, and the cost of that ruling is the same second headless library.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: a token switched to Linear gradient shows the preview, two draggable stop handles and two pickers. Dragging stop two from 1.0 to 0.75 moved the handle and the numeric field with it; picking on stop one committed #33c2ff into that stops colour. Editor suite 1049 across 85 files.

title: A binding no longer outlives its object, so deleting a readout does not disarm saving
detail: FIXED AT THE SERIALISER, not at the delete. A binding is keyed by its object id, so deleting the object left a key naming something the scene no longer had; serialiseThemeEnvelope then produced a document the validator refuses and every later save in that session threw with nothing in the UI saying so. The Starter binds 25 of its 52 objects, so deleting one sensor readout disarmed saving for the rest of the session while the row simply looked like it had vanished. snapshot now drops bindings whose key is not an object in the scene. WHY THERE AND NOT AT EACH DELETE: the keyboard, the layer list, the context menu, undo and any path added later all arrive at snapshot, so this cannot be the one that was forgotten, and it is a trust boundary — the serialiser no longer names an object that is not there, whatever removed it. A binding is meaningless without its object, so nothing is lost that the document could still use, and an author who re-adds an object with that id gets its reading back. THE ROWS OTHER TWO QUESTIONS ARE NOT ANSWERED and are still decisions: whether a save that throws should report itself rather than vanish, and whether a failed save leaves the document marked dirty so the author is warned on the way out. Both are separable from this and neither is fixed here.
check: Against a live host, the rows exact sequence: delete network-up, then File > Save to library. The host document now reads 51 objects with network-up absent, bindings 25 to 24, and no binding naming a missing object — and no pageerror. Red without the fix: the test fails with Invalid Fabric theme: Fabric object network-up is not in this scene, the exact error the row reported. Editor suite 1050 across 85 files.

title: A deleted object now disappears from the layer list, the canvas and the inspector together
detail: FIXED, and it was two subscriptions rather than one. A deletion fires no selection event — the active object is discarded first — so neither the bridge nor the selection inspector was told, and the row survived. Measured on the row own sequence: after Edit > Delete on network-up the canvas reported 51 objects and the host document agreed, but the layer list still showed 52 rows including network-up, and the inspector still read its name and geometry. So the three surfaces disagreed about what the document contained, and the row is right that this is one defect seen three ways. Both now subscribe to object:removed and object:added: the bridge, which republishes the layer projection, and the selection inspector, which re-binds its fields. After the same keystroke all three agree — 51 rows, no network-up, and the inspector empty. THE STUB WAS ALSO LYING, which is worth recording: bridge.dom.test.ts canvas stub answered getObjects but had no add or remove, so a test that deleted an object was still projecting from an array that still held it. A test written against that stub would have passed for the wrong reason — mine did, on the first attempt. The stub now has Fabric own add and remove, and the tests pin the republish rather than the projection, because layers() reads live and so was never the thing that was stale.
check: Live: Edit > Delete on network-up takes the layer list 52 to 51 with network-up gone, the canvas to 51 objects, and the inspector back to empty. Red without the subscription: both bridge tests fail. Editor suite 1052 across 85 files.
